name: India–Pakistan
value: Airspace bans to 24 Nov; no strikes
summary: India–Pakistan airspace bans run to 24 Nov; Indus treaty dispute continues; quiet as of 9 Nov with no strikes found
state: Pakistan's ban on Indian aircraft runs until 24 Nov after an extension on 17 Oct (Dawn). A Court of Arbitration rejected India's suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty on 31 Aug (Dawn). The latest exchange found was on 15–16 Oct, when India's defence minister warned of a bigger strike after any new attack and Pakistan's Foreign Office promised a forceful response (Express Tribune). The signal was quiet as of 9 Nov: searches found no new cross-border strike, mobilisation or Line of Control clash.
for_you: Flights between Europe and South Asia may take longer routes while the airspace bans last. FCDO travel advice is the official guide for travel near the Line of Control.
rubric_hit: Watch: treaty suspension (Indus Waters) still in dispute and reciprocal airspace bans in place; no cross-border strikes or mobilisation

sources.title: Indian airlines barred from using Pakistani airspace until Nov 24 as ban extended

why: Two nuclear-armed neighbours with a history of rapid escalation after terrorist attacks.
drivers: Kashmir attacks, Line of Control firing, water disputes (Indus), domestic politics.

rubric.watch: Ceasefire violations, a major terrorist attack with blame assigned, or treaty suspensions.
rubric.normal: Ceasefire holding along the Line of Control; no major attacks.
